text_blocks.snippet: The period of contagiousness for COVID-19 varies depending on factors such as the severity of illness and individual immune response.
According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), most people with COVID-19 are contagious for:

list.snippet: 5 days: from the onset of symptoms until 5 days after symptoms resolve (e.g., if symptoms start on a Monday, they are contagious until the following Saturday)
10 days: if they have moderate to severe illness

text_blocks.snippet: Individuals who test positive for COVID-19 but remain asymptomatic may still be contagious for up to 10 days from the date of their positive test.

It's important to note that these are general guidelines, and the actual period of contagiousness may be shorter or longer in some cases. If you have any concerns about your contagiousness, consult with a healthcare professional.
